name: bid_ask_imbalance_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when large institutional participants (FII desks, mutual fund TWAP algos) are working directional orders, each 5-second bar consistently closes near its high (buy-side pressure) or near its low (sell-side pressure) because continuous aggressive order flow absorbs the opposing side. When this bar-level imbalance sustains across a 1-minute EMA window, the institutional order is still active — large directional orders are typically only 40-60% filled at any 1-minute mark — predicting continuation of the NIFTY spot move over the next 30-90 seconds. We approximate the L2 bid-ask imbalance using OHLCV microstructure: bar_imbalance = (close - low) / (high - low) - 0.5, which captures the net buying vs selling pressure visible in each 5-second bar without requiring raw order book depth data.

indicators.name: bar_imbalance
indicators.purpose: OHLCV proxy for bid-ask imbalance. A bar closing near its high (+0.5) means buyers absorbed all sell-side flow; near its low (-0.5) means sellers dominated. At 5-second frequency this is a direct proxy for tick-by-tick order flow direction without requiring L2 data.

indicators.name: bar_imbalance_ema_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute EMA (12 bars × 5s) of bar imbalance. The original used EMA(3) on 1-min bars = 3 minutes; we compress to 1 minute because our hold time is 30-90 seconds. The signal trigger lookback should match the hold horizon — using a 3-minute signal to trade a 90-second move introduces excessive lag.

indicators.name: imbalance_zscore_60
indicators.purpose: Z-score of the 1-min EMA over a 5-minute baseline (60 bars). The original used a 20-bar z-score on 1-min bars = 20 minutes; we compress to 5 minutes because NIFTY's intraday microstructure regime (trending vs choppy) changes frequently and a 20-minute baseline would include stale order flow patterns. 5 minutes captures the current session microstructure while filtering noise.

indicators.name: vol_ratio_60
indicators.purpose: Relative volume over 5-minute baseline. High relative volume confirms that the imbalance is driven by genuine large-lot activity, not by random noise in thin bars. Matches the original's volume_ratio > 1.2 filter.

indicators.name: session_vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative(close * volume) / cumulative(volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP from 09:15 IST. Used as a directional bias filter: buy CE only when close > VWAP (bullish tape) and buy PE only when close < VWAP (bearish tape). Reduces counter-trend trades that have lower win rates.

buy_ce.confirmation: Z-score sustained above confirmation level for 2 prior bars to filter single-bar spikes

buy_pe.confirmation: Z-score sustained below confirmation level for 2 prior bars to filter single-bar spikes

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points = ~6 NIFTY spot points. If sustained order flow imbalance (1-min EMA z-score > 1.5) is genuine institutional pressure, NIFTY should not reverse 6+ spot points within the 30-90s hold window. A 6-point reversal on NIFTY within 90 seconds signals the imbalance was noise or already absorbed.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points = ~10 NIFTY spot points. When active institutional order flow is detected via 1-min BAI EMA, continuation typically extends 10-15 spot points before the order completes. Targeting 10 points captures the lower end of the distribution for a high win-rate at 1:1.67 R:R.

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; at VIX > 22, bid-ask spreads widen and OHLCV imbalance proxy becomes unreliable as gap-and-spike bars dominate
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; skip first 5 minutes (pre-open noise) and last 5 minutes (EOD forced exits)
filters.volume_filter: vol_ratio_60 > 1.2 (relative volume confirmation of institutional activity)
filters.trend_filter: close vs session VWAP for directional bias

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — OHLCV-based imbalance proxy is less precise than true L2 order book data, but more robust to spoofing. As NIFTY microstructure becomes more efficient at 5s resolution, z-score thresholds may need upward adjustment.

adaptation_notes: Original required real-time L2 order book data (5-level bid/ask depth) for individual NIFTY 50 stocks. This is unavailable in the 5s OHLCV pipeline and unreliable for index trading. Adaptation: (1) replaced L2 BAI with bar_imbalance = (close-low)/(high-low)-0.5 as OHLCV proxy — captures net buy/sell pressure in each 5s bar without depth data; (2) universe changed from NIFTY 50 constituent stocks to NIFTY index itself; (3) EMA lookback compressed from 3-min (original: EMA(3) on 1-min bars) to 1-min (EMA(12) on 5s bars) to match 30-90s hold horizon; (4) z-score window compressed from 20-min to 5-min (60 bars) for fresher regime baseline; (5) eliminated cross-sectional stock selection (this version trades only NIFTY index options).
weaknesses: OHLCV bar imbalance is a noisy proxy for true L2 order flow — it conflates direction of trades with intensity, and cannot distinguish large block trades from multiple small orders.
On very fast NIFTY moves (>10 pts in 5s), bar_imbalance is always ±0.5 (close at extreme), making z-score less informative.
2-bar confirmation introduces latency — by bar 3, some of the institutional order may already be filled, reducing residual continuation.
